chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) would greet the women, and they would return the greeting to him; and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would greet the women, and he disliked greeting the young woman among them, saying: 'I fear that her voice might please me, so what enters upon me [in terms of distraction/feeling] would be more than what I seek from the reward.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali (AS) dislike greeting young women?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the nuanced Shia jurisprudence regarding gender interaction, distinguishing between the general permissibility of greeting women and the specific caution advised against young women. Imam Ali’s (AS) reasoning highlights the concept of *khawf al-shughl* (fear of distraction), where excessive sensory pleasure might diminish the sincerity (*ikhlas*) and thus the spiritual reward of the act. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on guarding the heart from minor distractions to maintain pure devotion in daily rituals.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was so that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the women and they were returning the greeting upon him<sup>saww</sup>; and it was so that Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> would greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the women, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to dislike greeting (السَّلَامُ) upon the young ones from them, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying (it is so that): ‘One should be afraid that her voice might astound him, so what would enter upon him would be more than what he is seeking from the Recompense’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib’i ibn ‘Abd Allah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah would offer greeting of peace to women and they would respond to him. Amir al-Mu’ minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) would offer greeting of peace to women but he disliked offering it to the young women. He would say, ‘I fear their voice may attract me and a feeling may cause me more harm than the reward for offering the greeting of peace.’”
